questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: No aspects, I just chose the place that looked like could be fun.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy. Some of the information I had to seek and find out myself, but other than that, emails were sent with information regularly.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any assistance. There were information meetings in the beginning and of course emails, but not really anything other than that. We were assigned a buddy from the study destination, that was from that University in the beginning, which I found helpful in terms of meeting new people.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy, it was 5 minutes from campus, and was for students. (Broadgate Park Accommodation)

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It was basically on campus, just 5 minutes from there, so the difference was not really felt.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I arrived, and told them my name at the informative meeting for exchange students, they crossed me off, and that was it.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We had a contact person for exchange students.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was a bit confused about classes. I ended up registering for 4 classes (because of the credits I needed for my home university), which I found overwhelming, as we normally do 3 at most at my home university. I would have liked more information about classes as an exchange student.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I do not know, registation was not that hard. However, if you are a postgradstudent, and can do undergrad courses, I would recommend that, because I found out too late, that I could do all undergrad courses as a postgrad exchange student. If I would have known before going, I would have done all my courses undergrad, as I could have done 3 instead of 4, and gotten the credits I needed, without feeling overwhelmed.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: If I had known I could have done all BA classes, I would have done that. I felt there was too much material for the MA classes, when thinking about the amount of credits you got for the one class. I also did not think they took into consideration, that a student could have up to 3 other classes, than that one class. I liked the one BA class I had better, because the readings were proportionate. In terms of level, I would say my MA readings were generally harder to understand and longer, than my readings for my BA class.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The readings were very different and all online. At UCPH we normally have a book for the course that we can turn to and reference, which I prefer much more. Having different readings that say different things became confusing for me in the assessment period in terms of choosing and including the 'right' thing. Also, I would have difficulties multiple times when it came to access the readings that were listed.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. International Humanitarian Law
2. Equality and Discrimination in the Criminal Justice System
3. Economic and Social Rights
4. Philosophical Foundations of Criminal Justice

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend BA classes generally, as I found my one BA class more understandable than the MA ones. However, I enjoyed having Economic and Social Rights as well, because the teacher was very talented and made the course very interesting in terms of explaining and teaching us the material.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds, very impressed. Just a shame because I thought it was too expensive for me

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I tried out for the basketball team in the beginning, that was very fun.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go see other parts of the UK as well! It is beautiful! Brighton, London, Manchester, Peak District.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was not very hard.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just be yourself and be open to meeting new people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing challenging, just that british people tend to be much more talkative in the day-to-day life.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The kindness and openness

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Enjoy it, it goes by very fast!
I would recommend the BA classes
Be open to meeting new people

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not particularly.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: the friends I made and all the new things I learned about myself.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being far from my family and home, especially during the assessment period, where stress and anxiety tends to be high for me.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
